headline: Three-cycle target: the conic of special coefficients is real at first order but dies at second order, so it gives no larger Hodge locus (confirmed by an independent check, modulo two primes).

active.title: Three or more cycles: special coefficients
active.state: first-order conic confirmed; second-order obstruction confirmed (mod p); next steps open
active.summary: On an explicit quartic sixfold with three 3-planes in one P^4, the tangent space of the Hodge locus jumps on the six pairwise lines and on a conic determined by a cross-ratio of four points. Exact over QQ at a conic point. At second order the extra direction is obstructed (blind check, two primes): near such points the Hodge locus is no bigger than the locus where the planes persist. Next: non-linear configurations, sextic fourfolds, an exact second-order certificate.

recent.what: Second order on the conic: the extra direction is obstructed (blind check, two primes). First-order value exact over QQ; conic explained by a cross-ratio.
Blind check confirmed the conic of special coefficients (first order; exact at named points, mod p for the conic).
Three-cycle target: candidate conic of special coefficients found (exact at one instance); blind check started.

Survey of related work: one-cycle results of Kloosterman (arXiv:2104.14845) and Dan noted; Movasati's 2019 Fermat-surface tables cross-checked (1758 records agree at first order; 42 records differ at second order outside the range, unresolved).
Software package HodgeLociCI 0.1.0 and this discoveries registry published; one blind install check, all 28 findings fixed.
Discovery round closed: explicit families for coefficient -1 (sums of two determinants) and 1 (Pfaffians) on cubic sixfolds; no unexplained piece found for fake linear cycles on quartic sixfolds.
